title: Accelerating Sustainable Economic Convergence
subtitle: Infrastructure, Innovation and the Structural Transformation of Developing Economies

contribution: Operationalizes The Theory of Sustainable Economic Convergence—concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics—by specifying the practical infrastructure, innovation, financing, and industrial-transformation mechanisms that accelerate catch-up toward 2050 and 2100.
abstract: Accelerating Sustainable Economic Convergence is a flagship policy and mechanism monograph within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).

keyFindings.title: Accelerating sustainable convergence requires more than aggregate capital spending: it depends on expanding productive capabilities, modernizing physical and digital infrastructure, and accelerating clean-technology diffusion without reproducing polluting industrial pathways.
Coordinated deployment lifts the Developing-Economy Convergence Index from 40.5 (2025) to 74.0 by 2050 and 91.5 by 2100, raising annual TFP growth to 3.4–4.1% between 2025 and 2050.
Structural transformation shifts developing-economy output out of legacy polluting sectors (48% → 14% by 2050, 6% by 2075) into clean manufacturing (33–38%) and digital/modern services (38–44%).
Mobilizing $1.8T–$3.0T/yr in blended, domestic, and MDB-guaranteed capital delivers a 12.1x 25-year social benefit-cost ratio across the integrated infrastructure and innovation package.
